title: Frequently asked questions
body: Straight answers on storm damage, shingles, metal, torch-down rubber, and what a fair roof job looks like in East Texas.

faqs.question: What should I do if my roof is damaged by a severe storm in Gilmer or East Texas?
faqs.answer: If you suspect storm damage, stay safe by staying off the roof and call Raymond Hardin Roofing first at (903) 797-2756 before you call your insurance company. We will make a thorough inspection of the damage and give your insurance company complete information to help you receive the most complete coverage allowed by your policy.

faqs.question: How much experience does Raymond Hardin have in East Texas roofing?
faqs.answer: Raymond Hardin has been installing and repairing roofs in East Texas for over 40 years. He learned the trade working for other roofing companies starting when he was just 17 years old, and in 1995 he started Raymond Hardin Roofing in Gilmer, TX to offer the highest quality roofing service at the best price.

faqs.question: How do you protect my yard, landscaping, and pets during a roof tear-off?
faqs.answer: We take good care of our customers! Before we begin any tear-off work, we lay down tarps to control the mess and protect landscaping. During the roofing process, we use a rolling magnet daily to collect stray nails that might injure people or pets, and we replace all turbines, pipes, and stacks to give your entire roof a brand new look.

faqs.question: How do I know if I need a simple roof repair or a complete new roof?
faqs.answer: Signs that your roof is failing include: sagging or buckling decking, missing/lifting/curling shingles, shingle granules in gutters, dark mold or moss, exposed nails, interior ceiling water stains, points of daylight showing around chimneys or vents in a dark attic, or a roof that is 20+ years old. We perform a free inspection and give you an honest assessment.

faqs.question: Will you help me with permits and insurance payments in Gilmer, Longview, or Tyler?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. With our free estimate, you'll know the exact cost of your roof installation or repair. We take care of all the necessary permits and work with you when you're waiting for insurance payments.

faqs.question: Is Raymond Hardin Roofing licensed, bonded, insured, and BBB Accredited?
faqs.answer: Yes! Raymond Hardin Roofing is licensed, bonded, insured, and is a BBB Accredited Business serving Gilmer and all surrounding East Texas towns since 1995.

faqs.question: What is the difference between three-tab shingles and architectural shingles?
faqs.answer: Three-tab shingles are single-layer strips that provide a flat, uniform look and are budget-friendly. Architectural (dimensional or laminate) shingles are thicker and heavier, made from multiple layers sealed together to create a three-dimensional look with greater durability and a longer warranty.

faqs.question: Why is Torch-Down Rubber Roofing ideal for flat or low-pitch roofs?
faqs.answer: Water tends to puddle on flat or low-pitch roofs (common on commercial buildings, carports, patios, and older homes). Torch-down rubber consists of two or three layers of an asphalt and rubber compound heated to form a watertight seal that expands and contracts with East Texas temperatures without cracking—and without the awful smell of hot tar.

faqs.question: What are the benefits of installing a Metal Roof in East Texas?
faqs.answer: Metal roofing is durable, long-lasting, fire resistant, low maintenance, and available in a wide variety of colors. It reflects the sun's rays to reduce summer heat (and may qualify for energy-saving tax credits), and its cost is recovered in both roof lifespan and increased property value.

faqs.question: What is the difference between reroofing and a full roof replacement?
faqs.answer: Reroofing adds new roofing over existing shingles (allowed only once by building codes, and only if the decking is solid with no leaks or decay). Because major problems often recur with reroofing, a full tear-off and roof replacement—which averages a 105% return on investment—is usually the better choice.

faqs.question: What questions should I ask before letting any roofer on my roof?
faqs.answer: Always check: (1) How much experience they have with your specific roof material; (2) Whether they are licensed, bonded, and insured; (3) Local referrals and photos of past work; (4) BBB accreditation and verified reviews; (5) That they never use high-pressure storm-chaser sales tactics; (6) Clear material and workmanship warranties; and (7) True value and quality at a fair price.
